title: Stochastic Peaking Ensemble: Token Surge Simulation
content:
Purpose:
This sheet captures a set of stochastic ensemble simulations for short-window peak events (1m, 5m, 15m) across model classes and regions. The intent is to: 1) quantify required token/sec and QPS headroom under correlated-user burst regimes, 2) surface GPU-family mix sensitivity, and 3) propose operational safety margins and quick dispatch rules for hosted API.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
We ran 10,000 Monte Carlo scenarios combining random user cohorts, model mix shifts (chat-heavy vs embed-heavy), and correlated regional traffic spikes. Median 15m peak token/sec is 2.1M tokens/s; the 95th percentile is 5.6M tokens/s, and the 99.5th percentile reaches 8.9M tokens/s. When constrained to the current GPU fleet mix (A100-80GB slices + T4 fallback), estimated 95th percentile latency SLO violations occur if average batching remains below 1.8x baseline. To meet 99th percentile SLOs during correlated spikes, we recommend a dynamic 35% safety margin on token/sec capacity with model-class-aware reserved pools.

Simulation assumptions and parameters:
- Time windows simulated: 60s, 300s, 900s (1m, 5m, 15m)
- Number of runs: 10,000 stochastic draws per window
- User cohort models: small-app (~75k MAU), platform partner (~250k MAU), enterprise (10 large tenants)
- Request distributions: Poisson baseline with correlated multiplier (log-normal, mu=0.0..1.5, sigma=0.35)
- Model classes and token multipliers: chat-llm (x1), instruction-tuned (x0.85), longform (x2.8), embeddings (x0.15 per token unit)
- GPU families: A100-80GB (top perf), A10G/T4 (mid/low perf) simulated with effective tokens/sec factors [1.0, 0.38, 0.18] per card
- Batching model: baseline continuous batching rate observed in production (1.0x). We simulate degraded batching (0.6x) and improved batching (2.0x) to examine sensitivity.
- KV cache hit rates: 10% baseline, 40% high-cache scenario
- Network/regional failure modes: simulated 0.5% probability of cross-region egress throttling per run

Key results (aggregated by window):
- 1m window: median tokens/s = 1.9M, 95th = 4.2M, 99.5th = 7.1M
- 5m window: median tokens/s = 2.0M, 95th = 4.9M, 99.5th = 8.2M
- 15m window: median tokens/s = 2.1M, 95th = 5.6M, 99.5th = 8.9M
- QPS conversion (assumes average 25 tokens/request): median QPS ~84k, 95th QPS ~224k, 99.5th QPS ~356k

Sensitivity slices (short summary):
- GPU mix: moving 25% of capacity from A100->A10G increases 95th tokens/s requirement by ~42% to maintain same latency profile.
- Batching: improving batching from 1.0x to 2.0x reduces 95th token/sec requirement by ~38%. If batching falls to 0.6x, 95th token/sec demand increases ~55%.
- KV cache: raising cache hits from 10%->40% cuts peak tokens/sec by ~18% in chat-dominant scenarios.

Operational targets and safety margins (recommendations):
- Baseline target (product-ready): maintain 2.4M tokens/s provisioned per region as reserved capacity for steady-state plus small bursts (covers median + 15%).
- Headroom target (95th percentile resilience): provision 6.2M tokens/s per global ingress plane (region-aware routing to distribute to regional pools).
- Extreme tail buffer (99.5th preparedness): maintain conditional spill capability either via burst credits to dedicated fleets or cross-region fallback capacity totaling 9.5M tokens/s globally.
- Model-aware reserved pools: designate 25% of reserved capacity for longform/high-token workloads to avoid queueing that severely impacts tail latency for chat requests.
- Throttling policy: soft 95th throttles at application tier with degradation to embeddings-only for non-tiered traffic during sustained >10m spikes.

Regional allocation prescription (example split for global ingress):
- NA (North America): 40% of headroom pool -> 2.48M (95th target allocation)
- EU (Europe): 30% -> 1.86M
- APAC: 20% -> 1.24M
- RoW / LatAm / fallback: 10% -> 0.62M
Note: percentages tuned by observed historical peak share; weekly recalibration recommended.

GPU fleet dispatch heuristics (quick rules):
- First line: route chat-heavy requests to A100 pool; maintain prewarmed small slices for low-latency short queries.
- Second line: route instruction-tuned to mixed A100/A10G pools.
- Fallback: embeddings and background batch jobs to A10G/T4.
- Prewarmed buffer: maintain 5% of A100 inventory as prewarmed tiny-slices for sub-100ms cold-start SLOs.

Staffing and runbook notes:
- Ops shifts: on-call shift should be alerted when 5m sustained token rate exceeds 80% of 95th headroom; escalation to SRE lead at 90%.
- Playbook snippet: if observed 15m token rate > 95th and latency > 150ms p95, trigger: 1) auto-burst to dedicated fleet, 2) enable model-class routing to offload longform, 3) notify growth/partners of potential degraded experience.
- Drill cadence: quarterly chaos drills simulating correlated partner bursts; capture early-warning telemetry (token/s anomaly, KV cache hit drop, batching rate dip).

Action items and open questions (next steps):
- [Owner: Samir] Run a focused 100k-run simulation that includes extreme tail correlated network throttle scenarios (due 2026-03-18).
- [Owner: Maya] Produce a compact dashboard widget for Console showing live percentile banding (median/95/99.5) for tokens/s by region (P0).
- [Owner: Ethan] Propose pricing/burst-credit policy aligned with operational burst costs for dedicated customers (draft due 2026-04-01).
- Open question: whether to implement model-aware reserved pools as hard reservations (wasted capacity risk) or soft priority with eviction; need risk/cost analysis.

Appendix snippets (raw numbers):
- Example 95th headroom table (global): A100-equivalent cards required at 95th = 420 (baseline batch=1.0); if batching improves to 1.5x, required A100-equivalents fall to ~260.
- Cost sensitivity: switching 20% of traffic to A10G yields estimated additional infra cost of +18% to maintain p95 latency.

Notes to reviewers: this is a working simulation output. The ensemble harness and scripts are in linked_artifacts. Please flag any unrealistic user-behavior assumptions or missing failure modes we should add to the next iteration.

Short changelog:
- 2026-02-18: initial run and draft (Ethan)
- 2026-02-25: expanded regional splits and batching sensitivity (Maya)
